title: The Economic Importance of Motorcycles to Europe
gist: Oxford Economics, for ACEM, estimates EU+UK motorcycle-related activity supported €35.1bn GDP, 481,600 jobs and €20.6bn tax revenue in 2024, with a 2.30x indirect/induced multiplier. About half of EU motorcycle and parts output is exported, and a 5% car-to-motorcycle commuter shift is modelled to save 28m commuting days and 2.6Mt CO₂ a year.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics estimates motorcycle-related activity in the EU and UK supported €35.1 billion in GDP, 481,600 jobs and €20.6 billion in tax revenues in 2024, including supply-chain and induced spending.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Sizes a niche European manufacturing/leisure sector; useful baseline for lobbying weight on EU regulation and tariffs.

insights.claim: For every €1 of GDP generated directly by the EU and UK motorcycle sector, a further €2.30 is supported elsewhere in the economy, per Oxford Economics modelling.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: High multiplier strengthens industry's case for policy support; note consultant-for-client (ACEM) provenance.
insights.quote: For every €1 of GDP generated directly by the sector, a further €2.30 was supported elsewhere.

insights.claim: Around half of EU motorcycle and parts production was exported in 2024, making the European motorcycle industry heavily exposed to global trade conditions.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: European motorcycle makers carry high tariff/trade-war sensitivity; watch export-market tariff actions.

insights.claim: The ACEM-commissioned report argues trade barriers, growing competition and regulatory complexity constrain the European motorcycle industry's opportunities to invest and expand.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Signals industry lobbying agenda: trade liberalisation and regulatory simplification at EU level.

themes.theme: Motorcycles in urban mobility and emissions

insights.claim: Around 6.4 million people across the EU and the UK already commute by motorcycle.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Installed commuter base indicates addressable market for two-wheeler mobility products and policy.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics models that if 5% of EU and UK car commuters switched to motorcycles, annual savings would reach 28 million days of commuting time and 2.6 million tonnes of CO₂.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Scenario framing positions motorcycles as an urban decarbonisation/congestion tool in mobility plans; scenario not forecast.

insights.claim: The ACEM report frames motorcycles as complementary to public transport within urban mobility plans, reducing commuting times, operating costs, emissions and demand for urban space.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Watch whether city mobility plans adopt two-wheeler-friendly policies, a demand tailwind for makers.
